title: Add latest-only release workflow
description:
## Summary

Adds `.github/workflows/release.yml` — a `workflow_dispatch`-only workflow that replaces (rather than supplements) the Workbench version of every managed image and opens a PR against `main`.

- **Same-edition patches** use `bakery update version --target-version` to preserve pinned dependency versions (R / Python / Quarto).
- **Edition bumps** use `bakery create version` + `bakery remove version`, allowing fresh dependency resolution per `dependencyConstraints`.
- Three-pass README sync (`OLD_TAG` → `TAG_VERSION`, then display, then edition-conditional) keeps published version references in step with `bakery.yaml`.
- PR is authored via a GitHub App token so downstream PR workflows (`Lint`, `Production`, `Zizmor`) trigger normally.
- Security pattern matches the reference shared workflow: no `${{ }}` expressions inside any `run:` block; all values flow through `env:`.

## Configuration required before first run

The repository must have these secrets configured (reuse the existing `images-workbench` App or provision a new one):

- `APP_ID`
- `APP_PRIVATE_KEY`

## Test plan

The workflow cannot be invoked from a non-default branch until it merges, so smoke-testing happens after merge:

- [ ] **No-op run** — trigger with the version currently pinned in `bakery.yaml` (`gh workflow run release.yml -f version="$(bakery get version workbench-for-google-cloud-workstations)"`). Expect: capture step reports "Nothing to do." and all later steps skip.
- [ ] **Same-edition patch** — trigger with a bumped build identifier in the same edition (e.g. `2026.04.0+526.pro3`). Expect: `bakery update version` branch runs; PR body says "Same-edition patch: dependency pins preserved".
- [ ] **Edition bump** — trigger with the next edition (e.g. `2026.05.0+...`). Expect: `bakery create` + `bakery remove` branch runs; PR body says "Edition bump: dependencies re-resolved".

title: Adopt Bakery project structure for positron-sagemaker
description:
Phase 2 of the Positron on SageMaker productionization epic: move the image onto the standard Bakery layout — `bakery.yaml` registration, a Jinja2 `template/` directory, and a rendered `2026.07/` version directory — replacing the plain `image/` Docker build context from Phase 1.

- Registering the image in the root `bakery.yaml` lets the shared `bakery-build-pr.yml` PR workflow build it automatically, so the Phase 1 interim path-filtered job (`psm-interim.yml`) is removed.

title: Add update workflow for Positron version bumps
description:
Phase 6 (positron-sagemaker#15), the update-workflow deliverable — the only part of Phase 6 not blocked on `platform-infra#298` (Public ECR provisioning). Runs on `workflow_dispatch` and a daily schedule (a cheap version check, not an image build, unlike the weekly WGCW/WAML rebuild schedules).

- Detects a new Positron release from the CDN's `pwb` (Workbench) release manifest — no "server" manifest exists (confirmed 403), but the `pwb` and `server` release trains share the same version numbers even though this image installs a different artifact. Compares against `bakery.yaml`'s current pin with a version-aware max, not "first in the list."
- Also resolves the current `sagemaker-distribution` CPU tag in the same run, via ECR Public's anonymous registry token (no AWS credentials needed), and bumps the pinned `FROM` tag alongside the Positron bump if it's changed — the design posted as a comment on positron-sagemaker#15, rather than a separate poller or a new Bakery dependency type.
- Opens a PR via `bakery create version` + a GitHub App token (matching this repo's `release.yml` pattern, needed so the bot-created PR actually triggers `pr.yml`'s CI — the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot), with a rendered-file diff posted as a PR comment (`--diff-against`, matching `product-release.yml`'s pattern). Never auto-merges; requires human review.

Verified the detection + resolution logic against live data before writing the workflow, and validated the actual PR-creation output by replicating the workflow's steps locally (disposable test branch/PR, since a brand-new `workflow_dispatch` workflow can't be dispatched until it exists on the default branch) — caught and fixed two real bugs in the process: `PRODRIVERS_VERSION` wasn't carried forward by `bakery create version` (fixed at the source in positron-sagemaker-pro-drivers by making Pro Drivers install unpinned/always-latest instead), and a shellcheck SC2129 style issue.

This is one of three positron-sagemaker#15 deliverables — the build workflow and `release.yml` additions are still blocked on `platform-infra#298` and not part of this PR.

title: Add Goss test suite for image structure
description:
Phase 5 of the productionization epic: Goss test suite, written once now that macro adoption (Quarto, R, Pro Drivers) is final, against the final install logic rather than CDN-tarball-era paths that would've needed rewriting per phase.

Structural checks only — this image runs a full SageMaker Studio JupyterLab app, not a simple service dgoss can health-check by port/process, so there's no "wait" needed and no server to talk to. Runtime/launch behavior on the actual platform is Phase 7 (`platform-team#460`).

Covers every item in the issue checklist: `positron-server`/`quarto`/`R`/`uv`/`python` on PATH; Positron Server/Quarto/R versions match pinned values; the activation directory's owner/group; `Rprofile.site` contents; the AWS Toolkit extension file; no Jupyter kernelspec; `odbcinst.ini` driver entries + the Athena driver file; and the two env vars (`ODBCSYSINI`, `JSP_POSITRON_LAUNCHER_DISABLED`).

Also cross-referenced against the prototype repo's docs (`README.md`, `docs/design-native-image.md`), which surfaced two more build-time-substitution checks worth adding: `enforced-settings.json`'s Bedrock model placeholder actually got substituted, and the baked `aws-config` credential-bridge profile exists.

title: Install Pro Drivers via apt instead of CDN .deb
description:
Register the Posit Pro apt repository (`apt.setup_posit_repo("pro")`) and install the `rstudio-drivers` apt package instead of downloading the fixed-distribution-id `.deb` bundle directly from the CDN. Phases 4a and 4b of the productionization epic, combined into one PR — 4a's repo registration has no independently verifiable behavior on its own (the spike already proved apt registration is safe), so splitting it from the driver install it exists to support would just add an inert intermediate PR.

- Removes the `PRODRIVERS_VERSION` build `ARG` and the `7C152C12` CDN distribution id entirely — the driver version is now tracked as a `bakery.yaml` custom value (`PRODRIVERS_VERSION`) rather than a Dockerfile `ARG`, since Bakery's typed dependency system has no driver/ODBC dependency kind the way it does for R/Python/Quarto.
- Verified against the pinned base image: `rstudio-drivers=2026.04.0` (same version the CDN bundle pinned) is available from the `pro` repo verbatim, with a byte-identical `/opt/rstudio-drivers/` layout and `odbcinst.ini.sample` content, and registering the repo doesn't disturb conda.

title: positron-sagemaker: consolidate plain-apt installs into one layer
description:
## Summary

Follow-on to #58: consolidates the scattered plain-apt installs into a single early layer and strips redundant apt work from the surrounding blocks.

**Stacked on #58** (`reorder-layers-caching`). Both were rebased onto `main` after #54 and #57 merged. Review/merge #58 first; this diff shows only the apt changes on top of it.

No change to *what* gets installed — the set of apt-installed packages is identical to #58's rendering (verified: nothing dropped, added, or duplicated).

## Before

Four blocks each drove apt independently:

| Block | apt work |
|-------|----------|
| R block | `apt-get update` + install `libzmq3-dev libuv1t64 libwebpmux3` |
| Quarto | open-repo `setup.deb.sh` (implicit update) + install `quarto` |
| Pro Drivers | pro-repo `setup.deb.sh` (implicit update) + **another** `apt-get update` + install `unixodbc unixodbc-dev rstudio-drivers` |
| AWS Toolkit (volatile) | `apt-get update` + install `unzip` |

That's ~5 `apt-get update` runs (3 explicit + 2 in the repo setup scripts), an `apt-get update` inside the frequently-rebuilt AWS Toolkit layer, and a **redundant double-update** in the drivers block (the pro `setup.deb.sh` already updates, then `apt.install()` updated again).

## After

- **New `# --- System packages (apt) ---` layer** near the top installs every plain Ubuntu-repo package in one shot: `libzmq3-dev libuv1t64 libwebpmux3 unixodbc unixodbc-dev unzip`. One `apt-get update` for all of them.
- **R block** → pure `r-install`, no apt.
- **Pro Drivers** → installs only `rstudio-drivers`, via `apt.install(update=False)` so it reuses the index the pro `setup.deb.sh` just refreshed (kills the redundant second update). `unixodbc`/`-dev` now come from the System packages layer.
- **AWS Toolkit (volatile)** → pure `curl` + unpack, **no apt at all**, so a toolkit version bump never re-runs apt.

Net: **one explicit `apt-get update`** (was three), fewer layers touching apt, and the volatile ARG-gated layers are apt-free.

## Correctness / safety

- Every `apt-get update` still lives in the **same `RUN`** as its install (the `apt.install()` macro cleans `/var/lib/apt/lists/*` per layer, so a later install can never read a stale index).
- `unixodbc` moving earlier is safe: it's present before both the drivers install and the R `odbc` drift check (now a goss test — see #57) that needs `libodbc.so.2`. Comments updated to reflect the new provenance.
- `bakery hadolint run`: no new findings.
- Package set verified identical to #58's rendering.

## Considered but not done

Merging **Quarto (open repo) + Pro Drivers (pro repo)** into a single Posit-repo layer was considered. Rejected for now: they pull from different repos with independent version cadences (quarto pinned, drivers unpinned/latest), each `setup.deb.sh` runs its own update regardless, and combining them couples two unrelated version bumps into one cache layer for marginal gain. Kept modular.

title: positron-sagemaker: reorder layers stable -> volatile for caching
description:
## Summary

Reorders `positron-sagemaker/2026.08/Containerfile.ubuntu2404` (and its template) so a routine version bump invalidates as little Docker build cache as possible.

**Rebased onto `main`** now that #54 (apt closure) and #57 (move-r-verify-to-goss) have merged. Targets `main` directly.

No executable content changes from the reorder itself: the set of non-comment lines equals `main`'s minus the verify block (see below). Only block order, `ARG` placement, and comments differ. Rendered from the template via `bakery update files`.

## The problem

The Positron Server download is gated on `ARG POSITRON_VERSION` — the most frequently bumped input in this image, since it tracks each Positron release. It previously sat near the **top** of the file, above the expensive toolchain. Under BuildKit, a changed `ARG` busts the `RUN` that consumes it **and every layer below it**, so each Positron version bump re-ran the entire R toolchain — including the multi-minute `install.packages(tidyverse, ...)` layer — plus Quarto, the ODBC drivers, and pip. None of those actually changed.

## The reordering (stable → volatile)

| Order | Section header | Change frequency |
|-------|----------------|------------------|
| 1 | `# --- R via r.j2 ...` (+ symlinks, Rprofile.site, package install) | stable / slowest |
| 2 | `# --- Quarto ...` | stable |
| 3 | `# --- Posit Professional Drivers (ODBC) ...` | stable |
| 4 | `# --- jupyter-server-proxy stack + Python tooling ...` | stable |
| 5 | `# --- Remove Jupyter kernelspecs ...` | stable |
| 6 | `# --- Positron proxy config ...` (COPY + JupyterLab asserts) | config |
| 7 | `# --- Positron Server ...` (`ARG POSITRON_VERSION`) | **volatile** |
| 8 | `# --- AWS Toolkit ...` (`ARG AWS_TOOLKIT_VERSION`) | volatile |
| 9 | `# --- Posit Assistant: Amazon Bedrock ...` (`ARG POSITRON_BEDROCK_MODEL`) | volatile |
| 10 | baked default AWS profile (`COPY aws-config`) | volatile |

Net effect: a Positron version bump (the common case) rebuilds only steps 7–10 (download + unzip + copies + sed), leaving the R/Quarto/driver/pip layers cached.

## Secondary change: ARG placement

Each `ARG` moves down to sit immediately above the single `RUN` that consumes it (`POSITRON_VERSION` → Positron Server; `AWS_TOOLKIT_VERSION` → AWS Toolkit; `POSITRON_BEDROCK_MODEL` → the `sed`). This makes each ARG's cache blast radius obvious. `USER root` moves up to just after `FROM`.

## Interaction with #57 (move-r-verify-to-goss) + a rendered-file fixup

#57 removed the "Verify R packages' system libraries" **build layer** in favor of a goss test, so this reorder no longer moves that block — it's simply gone, and the ordering comment notes the check now lives in `test/goss.yaml`.

#57 edited the templates but did **not** re-render the version files, so `main`'s rendered files were left stale. Re-running `bakery update files` here completes that render:
- drops the now-removed verify `RUN` block from `2026.08/Containerfile.ubuntu2404`, and
- adds the `r-packages-system-libraries-resolve` check to `2026.08/test/goss.yaml`.

That goss content is #57's already-merged template, not new here — it just wasn't rendered yet.

## Load-bearing orders preserved (documented inline)

- **R package install** follows **R install → symlinks → Rprofile.site**.
- **AWS Toolkit** follows the **Positron Server** extract (it unpacks into the server's `extensions/` dir).

## Verification

- `bakery update files` re-renders the committed files from the templates.
- Exec-line `diff` vs. `main`: identical once the verify block is excluded.
- `bakery hadolint run`: no new findings.

title: Document why Bakery python.j2 macros don't apply to positron-sagemaker
description:
## Summary

Investigated applying Bakery's `python.j2` macros to the Python install(s)
in `positron-sagemaker`, per the pattern used in
`workbench-for-google-cloud-workstations` and `workbench-for-microsoft-azure-ml`.
Conclusion: **the macros don't apply to this image**, so instead this just
documents why and confirms the existing install already follows best
practice for layer size.

## Why `python.j2` doesn't fit

`positron-sagemaker` builds on the `sagemaker-distribution` base image,
whose Python is managed by the base's own **conda `base` env** at
`/opt/conda` — not a Bakery/uv-managed CPython under `/opt/python/{version}`.

Every macro in `python.j2` (`build_stage`, `install_packages`,
`pip_install_command`, `get_version_directory`, etc.) assumes that
uv-managed `/opt/python/{version}` layout and passes `--break-system-packages`
to pip, neither of which applies here. Bakery also ships no
`conda.j2`/`mamba.j2` macro module to reach for instead — confirmed by
inspecting every macro file Bakery provides (`apt.j2`, `dnf.j2`, `goss.j2`,
`python.j2`, `quarto.j2`, `r.j2`) and by testing against the pinned base
image (`public.ecr.aws/sagemaker/sagemaker-distribution:4.4.0-cpu`), where
`/opt/python` doesn't exist and Python/pip resolve to `/opt/conda/bin`.
This matches `bakery.yaml`, which declares no `python` dependency for this
image (unlike the two images above that do use `python.j2`).

## Best-practice check (layer size)

Verified empirically against the pinned base image that the existing
`pip install --no-cache-dir ...` line already satisfies the intent behind
`python.j2`'s `install_packages()` `clean` param: running it leaves **no**
pip cache directory (`~/.cache/pip`, `/root/.cache/pip`) and **no** leftover
wheel/build artifacts under `/tmp`. No further cleanup was needed to avoid
inflating the layer.

## Changes

- Added an explanatory comment block above the `pip install` `RUN` in
  `positron-sagemaker/template/Containerfile.ubuntu2404.jinja2` documenting
  the above.
- Regenerated `positron-sagemaker/2026.07/Containerfile.ubuntu2404` via
  `bakery update files` to keep the rendered file in sync.

Comment-only change — no build behavior is modified.

## Validation

- `bakery hadolint run --image-name positron-sagemaker`: 0 errors, same 4
  pre-existing warnings as this branch's tip (none new).
- `bakery build --image-name positron-sagemaker`: full image build succeeds;
  the `pip install` layer is 83.5MB with no cache bloat, matching the
  empirical no-cache-dir test.

## Base branch note

This targets `feat/push-positron-sagemaker-public-ecr` (#52), which is still
open, since this branch was cut from it and that keeps this diff scoped to
just the documentation change described above.

title: positron-sagemaker: close apt install layers with clean
description:

title: positron-update: replace old version instead of leaving both pinned
description:
## Summary

`positron-update.yml`'s "Create version" step always called
`bakery create version positron-sagemaker ... --force`, which renders
the new version but never removes the old one — so every daily
Positron bump left a stale version directory checked into
`bakery.yaml`/the image tree, unlike `release.yml`'s handling of the
Workbench images.

This aligns the two workflows:

- Same-edition bump: `bakery update version` patches the existing
  version in place (target-version = old version), preserving the
  pinned quarto/R dependency resolution — matching release.yml's
  in-place patch path.
- Edition bump: `bakery create version` (new subpath, re-resolves
  `dependencyConstraints`) followed by `bakery remove version` for the
  old one — matching release.yml's edition-bump path.

Since `bakery update version` has no `--diff-against` flag (the old
version it patches in place stops existing as a separate directory),
the rendered-diff comment content is now captured via `git diff --
positron-sagemaker` after the replace step instead, which works for
either branch.

## Testing

- `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/positron-update.yml'))"` — YAML parses.
- pre-commit hooks (actionlint, yaml check, etc.) passed on commit.
- Not run end-to-end (requires the scheduled workflow's GitHub App
  token/secrets); reasoned through both branches against `bakery --help`
  output for `create version` / `update version` / `remove version`.

title: feat(positron-sagemaker): support AWS License Manager licensing
description:
## Why

`positron-server` 2026.08+ can take its licensing verdict from an external client named by `POSITRON_LICENSE_MANAGER_PATH` (posit-dev/positron#15538, merged). For SageMaker that client is `license-manager-aws-sagemaker` from `rstudio/licensing-clients`, which checks a seat out of AWS License Manager under the Space's execution role — the same entitlement path RStudio on SageMaker already uses.

The server-side support landed, but **nothing in this image passes the variable**, and per that PR the License Manager path only takes precedence when the path is actually provided. So images built today still license via signing key + Secrets Manager.

Verified against a live domain (`d-tbo1cijoenrj`, us-east-2) running `positron-sagemaker-preview:2026.09.0-108`:

- CloudTrail: **zero** `CheckoutLicense` events
- CloudTrail: 40 `GetSecretValue` calls on `positron-signing-key` / `positron-license`, principal `SageMaker`, both read in the same second — the `jupyter_server_config.py` signature
- Neither `2026.08/Containerfile.ubuntu2404` nor `template/` sets `POSITRON_LICENSE_MANAGER_PATH`

## What this does

- **Containerfile** (template + generated): optionally installs the licensing client, behind `LICENSE_MANAGER_CLIENT_URL` and `LICENSE_MANAGER_CLIENT_SHA256`. Both default to empty, so a build that doesn't set them produces the current image.
- **jupyter_server_config.py** (template + generated): when the client binary is present *and* executable, exports `POSITRON_LICENSE_MANAGER_PATH` and `LM_LOG_FILE` into the `positron-server` spawn env. Otherwise falls through to the existing signing-key path, unchanged.

The presence check is deliberate — `POSITRON_LICENSE_MANAGER_PATH` pointing at a missing binary makes `positron-server` fail immediately rather than fall back, so the variable is only set once the client really exists.

## Open question — I need the client's distribution URL

**This is why it's a draft.** I couldn't find where `license-manager-aws-sagemaker` is published. The positron PR's example pulls it from a local build context, `rstudio/licensing-clients` has no releases, and my guesses at `cdn.posit.co` / `cdn.rstudio.com` both 403. Rather than invent a URL and a sha256, I left them as build args.

If you tell me the canonical endpoint I'll set the defaults and drop the opt-in guard.

Also worth confirming: is `POSITRON_LICENSE_MANAGER_PATH` the intended entrypoint on the Positron side? posit-dev/positron#15538 flags that as an open question, and the client's own README only documents the RStudio wiring (`server-license-manager-path` in `rserver.conf`).

## Follow-up, deliberately not in this PR

Removing the signing-key path from `jupyter_server_config.py` (~`_load_signing_key_pem`, the `.lic` install, `license-manager verify`, `_mint_license_token`, and the `POSITRON_LICENSE_KEY=` injection). Leaving it is harmless while License Manager takes precedence, but it still calls `GetSecretValue` on every spawn and raises when the secrets are absent — so it has to come out before "no secrets to store or rotate" is true. Safer as a second step, after a real build confirms checkout works.

## Testing

Local, since I can't build without the client URL:

- `python3 -m ast` parses both copies of `jupyter_server_config.py`
- The env-splice logic was exercised for both command shapes `setup_positron_server()` produces (`/usr/bin/env`-prefixed and bare binary) — the prefix is not duplicated and `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` is preserved
- The new `RUN` block passes `bash -n`, and with `LICENSE_MANAGER_CLIENT_URL=""` it exits 0 as a no-op
- Template and generated `jupyter_server_config.py` are byte-identical

**Not done:** no container build, and `bakery` isn't installed here, so I hand-applied the change to `2026.08/` to match `template/`. Please regenerate to confirm they agree.

## Verifying once the client is installed

Both signals flip cleanly:

- `CheckoutLicense` starts appearing in CloudTrail on each Positron launch
- `GetSecretValue` on `positron-signing-key` / `positron-license` stops

Then delete the two secrets as a negative control — Positron should still start.

title: Add internal ECR override registry for positron-sagemaker dev builds
description:
## What

Adds a second dev-build destination for the `positron-sagemaker` image: an
internal ECR repo, `935931255537.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/positron-sagemaker`,
alongside the existing `ghcr.io/posit-dev/positron-sagemaker-preview` preview repo.

## Why environments

The new ECR repo needs its own AWS role (different account/permissions than
the role used to push the production image to `public.ecr.aws`). Rather than
adding a second ad-hoc secret name, or continuing to share one repo-level
`AWS_ROLE` secret across both the production and development workflows, this
splits `AWS_ROLE` across two GitHub Environments:

- `production` — used by `positron-sagemaker.yml`; role can only push to the
  customer-facing public ECR repo.
- `development` — used by `development-positron-sagemaker.yml`; role can
  only push to the internal preview ECR repo.

Both environments are restricted to the `main` branch (reinforcing the
workflows' existing `github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'` guards) with no
approval/reviewer rules, since these run on unattended schedules/dispatches.

Both environments and their `AWS_ROLE` secrets already exist in the repo
(set up out-of-band), and the old repo-level `AWS_ROLE` secret has been
removed, so this PR only needs to wire the workflows/config up to match.

## Changes

- `bakery.yaml`: add the new ECR host as a second `overrideRegistries` entry
  for `positron-sagemaker`'s `devVersions`.
- `development-positron-sagemaker.yml`: add `environment: development`, plus
  `Configure AWS credentials` / `Login to Amazon ECR` steps gated the same as
  the existing `Push` step. Updated the header comment, which previously
  (and now incorrectly) said this workflow needed no AWS credentials.
- `positron-sagemaker.yml`: add `environment: production` to the `build` job

title: positron-sagemaker: add development image build workflow
description:
Adds daily and on-demand development builds of `positron-sagemaker` against the Positron **daily** channel, mirroring what `images-workbench` does for `workbench-positron-init`.

Trigger is `workflow_dispatch` (leave `version` empty for the latest daily, or pin an exact one e.g. `2026.09.0-108`) plus a `schedule` at **08:30 UTC** daily.

## What was missing

Three pieces had to be added — this wasn't just a workflow file:

1. **`bakery.yaml`** gains a `devVersions` block for `positron-sagemaker` (it had only pinned `versions:`). `overrideRegistries` points dev builds at `ghcr.io/posit-dev/positron-sagemaker-preview`, so an unreleased daily can never reach the customer-facing `public.ecr.aws` repo — which is also why this workflow needs no AWS credentials.
2. **The Containerfile template** hardcoded the `releases` CDN path segment. Now driven by `POSITRON_CHANNEL`, defaulting to `releases` so pinned-version builds are byte-for-byte unchanged in behaviour.
3. **The workflow** itself.

## Why the channel is rendered, not a build arg

`workbench-positron-init` passes `POSITRON_CHANNEL` as a `--build-arg`. That does **not** work here: `ImageTarget.build_args` is gated on `isMatrixVersion`, and this image has no `matrix`, so its dev versions render to an ephemeral `.dev-<version>/` dir with `args: {}` (confirmed in the bake plan). Jinja rendering of `values` is unconditional, so baking the channel into the rendered `ARG` default is what actually works. It stays an `ARG`, so local `--build-arg` override still works.

## Two behaviours worth reviewer attention

**Cross-flavor version discovery.** Bakery resolves Positron dailies from the *pwb* manifest, while this image downloads the *server* flavor. Both are published from the same commit under the same version string, so pwb discovery is a valid proxy — verified both tarballs return HTTP 200 at `2026.09.0-108`. It is an assumption that could silently break, so it's called out in `bakery.yaml`.

**The workflow forwards the *dispatched* dev-spec, not the resolved version.** My first pass had the matrix job pin its resolved version for the build job, to close a mid-run daily-rollover race. Testing showed a dev-spec sets `version_override`, and bakery then suppresses the floating `:daily` tags *even when the pinned version is the channel head* — so that design would have silently stopped default runs from publishing `:daily`. Forwarding the dispatched spec preserves it. The cost is that the build job re-resolves independently; a daily landing mid-run fails **loudly** (`No image targets matching ...`, exit 1) rather than building a mismatched version.

Tag behaviour, verified via `bakery build --plan`:

| Run | Tags |
|---|---|
| default (latest daily) | `2026.09.0`, `2026.09.0-108`, `…-ubuntu-24.04`, **`daily`**, `daily-ubuntu-24.04` |
| pinned `2026.09.0-107` | `2026.09.0`, `2026.09.0-107`, `…-ubuntu-24.04` (no `daily` — correctly not moved) |

## Scheduled-run handling

`schedule` events carry no inputs, which is load-bearing in two places:
- `channel` falls back to `'daily'` — bakery **hard-errors** on an empty `--dev-channel` (`'' is not one of 'release', 'preview', 'daily'`), so a scheduled run would otherwise fail at the matrix job.
- The push gate keys off `github.event_name == 'schedule'` rather than the unset `push` input, since publishing the new daily is the point of the schedule.

08:30 UTC was chosen because Positron publishes dailies in the evening UTC (~18:30), so the run picks up the previous evening's build rather than racing the publish. It also lands after this repo's Positron version check (04:30), clear of the weekly specialized-hour rebuilds (03:45–04:45 Sunday), and in the same 07–09 UTC band `images-workbench` uses for its daily dev builds.

## Verification

Run locally against real CDN state:

- Dev matrix resolves `2026.09.0-108`, `dev: true`, `linux/amd64`; explicit pin and `--dev-channel daily` filter both resolve correctly.
- Rendered dev Containerfile: `ARG POSITRON_VERSION=2026.09.0-108`, `ARG POSITRON_CHANNEL=dailies`, and the resulting CDN URL returns HTTP 200.
- Goss version assertion renders correctly for a daily: `/^Positron: 2026.09.0 build 108$/`.
- All dev tags target the ghcr preview repo only; no `public.ecr.aws` tags.
- Production path unaffected: matrix still resolves `2026.08.1-2` and the re-rendered `2026.08/Containerfile.ubuntu2404` still resolves `releases`.
- `pre-commit` (incl. `actionlint` + `zizmor`) passes.

## Before merging

The `positron-sagemaker-preview` ghcr package will be created on first push and defaults to **private** — it likely needs visibility/permissions set, as `workbench-positron-init-preview` presumably did.

Not added, since they weren't requested: a `cache` input like `development-positron.yml` has, and a `push:`-on-merge trigger.

title: session-complete: add self-contained Workbench session image
description:
## Why

On Kubernetes, Workbench assembles a session container from two images at launch: `workbench-session-init` copies the subset of `/opt/session-components` that the requested `PWB_SESSION_TYPE` needs into an `emptyDir`, which the `workbench-session` container sees at `/usr/lib/rstudio-server`.

Some consumers can't run an init container. The long-standing answer for them is [`r-session-complete`](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-docker-products/tree/main/r-session-complete), which installs all of Workbench into a single image so the components are simply present. That image is built on `product-base-pro`, not on the modern `workbench-session` base.

This adds the same idea on the current base: a `workbench-session` image with a full Workbench install layered on top, so Workbench can launch sessions from it with no init container.

The Helm chart already anticipates this shape — `components.enabled: false` is documented as "change `session.image.repository` to `rstudio/r-session-complete` to use the classic all-in-one session image instead." This image is the `workbench-session`-based equivalent of that sentence.

> [!NOTE]
> Installing all of Workbench to obtain the session components is **not** the efficient way to do this, and this PR doesn't claim otherwise. `workbench-session-init` exists precisely to ship just those components and remains the recommendation on Kubernetes. The README says this in an `[!IMPORTANT]` at the top.

## What this does

Adds a `session-complete` image: Ubuntu 26.04, `linux/amd64`, Standard and Minimal variants.

- **`bakery.yaml`** — new image entry. No `soci` option (see below), no goss `options` since a session image starts no long-running service of its own.
- **`template/Containerfile.ubuntu2604.jinja2`** — `workbench-session` base + Workbench install.
- **`template/scripts/install_workbench.sh.jinja2`** — port of the `images-workbench` script.
- **`template/test/goss.yaml.jinja2`** — 87 checks per variant.
- **`session-complete/README.md`**.
- **`.github/workflows/session-complete.yml`** — build, test, push to `ghcr.io`.
- **`.github/workflows/release.yml`, `.github/workflows/pr.yml`** — wire the image into version bumps and size PR CI for it.

### CI

`session-complete.yml` is modelled on `waml.yml`: matrix → build → goss → push, pushing on merges to `main`, weekly scheduled rebuilds, and `workflow_dispatch` from `main`. `ghcr.io` is the only registry for this image, so unlike WGCW and positron-sagemaker there's no cloud provider auth and no `id-token: write`.

Scheduled **05:15 Sunday**, last in the specialized sequence (positron-sagemaker 03:45, WGCW 04:15, WAML 04:45). Two constraints drove the slot: it layers on `workbench-session`, so it must run after that base is rebuilt by `images-workbench`'s Session Images workflow at 03:45, and it's the largest build in the repo, so it goes last and absorbs the window before the daily builds start at 07:45.

**`release.yml` needed this image added, not just as tidiness.** `bakery update version` is driven by the `IMAGES` list, but the README rewrite that follows is a repo-wide `find . -name 'README.md' -exec sed`. An image absent from `IMAGES` therefore still gets its README rewritten, and ends up advertising a Workbench version `bakery.yaml` never moved it to. Adding it keeps the two in step, and I extended the comment on the lockstep assumption so the next person adding a Workbench-pinning image here sees the coupling.

All three managed images are currently on `2026.08.1+195.pro1`, so the `IMAGES` lockstep precondition holds.

**`pr.yml`** gets `amd64-builder: "ubuntu-latest-8x"` — see the reservation below.

### The one deliberate deviation from the upstream install script

`images-workbench` curls a codename-pinned deb from `download2.rstudio.org/server/<codename>/<arch>/...`. This installs `rstudio-server` from the **Posit pro apt repository the base image already has configured** instead:

```shell
apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends "rstudio-server=${WORKBENCH_VERSION}"
```

The deb then always matches the base OS with no codename→URL table to keep in sync, and apt verifies the repo signature rather than the script checking a hand-maintained sha256. Adding another OS target later needs no change to the script.

### `libcap2` is an undeclared dependency of the Workbench deb

`rsession` and 22 other binaries under `/usr/lib/rstudio-server` link against `libcap.so.2`, but `rstudio-server`'s `Depends` is `rrdtool, libssl-dev, psmisc, libclang-dev, libsqlite3-0, lsb-release, sudo, libpq5, libc6` — no `libcap2`. **Installing the deb's declared dependencies is not sufficient to get a working `rsession`.**

This is invisible in the two places you'd expect to catch it. The Standard variant's package set pulls `libcap2` in incidentally, and `r-session-complete`'s `product-base-pro` base already has it. On **Minimal** it's absent, and the image builds perfectly cleanly then fails at session exec time:

```
/usr/lib/rstudio-server/bin/rsession: error while loading shared libraries:
libcap.so.2: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

The Containerfile installs `libcap2` explicitly. A new `workbench-binaries-shared-libs-resolve` goss check `ldd`-sweeps the whole install so the next such gap fails in CI rather than at a user's first session launch. `libR.so` is excluded by design — it's genuinely resolved at launch via `bin/r-ldpath`, which the adjacent `rsession-reports-pinned-workbench-version` check exercises.

**This is probably worth an upstream packaging bug against `rstudio-server`.** Happy to file it if it isn't already known.

### Other things worth knowing

**The component layout differs from the init-container form.** The `workbench-session-init` tarball nests per-distro binaries under `bin/jammy/`, `bin/resolute/`, etc.; the deb installs a single flat set at `bin/`. Anything reading these paths must expect the flat form.

**The postinst handles the NSS symlink itself,** repointing `libnss_pwb.so.2` at the flat `bin/libnss_pwb.so` and re-adding `pwb` to `nsswitch.conf`, so the script doesn't. It does leave the base's zero-byte `bin/resolute/libnss_pwb.so` placeholder behind, which the script removes (guarded, `rmdir` not `rm -rf`) — a stray zero-byte `libnss_pwb.so` is exactly what someone debugging NSS would mistake for the live module.

**`amd64`-only is a technical constraint, not just scoping.** The postinst hardcodes the multiarch triplet:

```shell
ln -sf /usr/lib/rstudio-server/bin/libnss_pwb.so /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnss_pwb.so.2
```

On `arm64` that writes to a path the loader doesn't read, silently leaving `libnss_pwb.so.2` pointed at the base's zero-byte placeholder and the `pwb` module inert. Documented in `bakery.yaml` and the README.

**No server state is baked in.** With no init system in the build container the postinst falls through to its sysv branch, creating inert `/etc/init.d/rstudio-*` and `/etc/rc{2,3,4,5}.d/S01rstudio-*` links — same artifacts `r-session-complete` produces from the same postinst. What matters is that the script patches out the service-start and license-init steps, and goss asserts no secure cookie key, launcher keypair, session RPC key, or `rstudio.sqlite` is present.

**Two Quarto installations, deliberately.** `quarto` on `PATH` resolves to the base's `/opt/quarto` (the version Bakery pins and tests); the deb's bundled copy stays at `/usr/lib/rstudio-server/bin/quarto` for the session components. This differs from `r-session-complete`, which symlinks the bundled copy onto `PATH`.

## Testing

`bakery dgoss run --image-name session-complete` — **174/174 passing, 87 per variant**, both Standard and Minimal on Ubuntu 26.04. `rsession --version` reports the pinned `2026.08.1+195.pro1` in both.

`pre-commit run --all-files` clean repo-wide, including ShellCheck, actionlint, and zizmor on the new and modified workflows. Re-rendering from templates is byte-identical (idempotent).

For the CI changes specifically:

- `bakery ci matrix --quiet --dev-versions exclude --matrix-versions exclude session-complete` — the exact command the new workflow's `matrix` job runs — returns valid JSON: `[{"image":"session-complete","version":"2026.08.1+195.pro1","dev":false,"platform":"linux/amd64"}]`.
- **Both `release.yml` bump paths were run against scratch checkouts**, not reasoned about. The same-edition patch (`bakery update version --target-version`) moves all three images and, after the repo-wide README sed, leaves `session-complete/README.md` at `2026.08.2-196.pro1` matching `bakery.yaml`'s `2026.08.2+196.pro1` — the desync this fixes. The edition bump (`bakery create version --subpath --mark-latest` then `bakery remove version`) correctly produces `session-complete/2026.11/` with the version propagated into both Containerfiles, the install script, and the goss assertions, and removes `2026.08/`.

What I have **not** done is run the new workflow. Its build/test/push steps are copied from `waml.yml` and the matrix command is verified, but the runner label, GHCR push, and Slack notification only get exercised on merge.

I checked the suite isn't vacuous rather than trusting a green run: sabotaging the `libnss_pwb.so.2` symlink failed exactly the 3 relevant checks while the other 84 passed. That also exposed a weak test of my own — `ldd` on an empty file reports no missing libraries, so `libnss-pwb-loadable` originally passed against the zero-byte placeholder. It now checks ELF magic first.

The `libcap2` bug above was caught by this suite on the Minimal variant, not by inspection.

## The one thing I couldn't verify

**`pr.yml` now requests `ubuntu-latest-8x` for amd64 builds, up from the `ubuntu-latest-4x` default.** That workflow builds every image in `bakery.yaml` on every PR, so it's sized for the largest, and this image is ~15 GB built on top of a ~7 GB base pull, with `--load` before the goss run.

Two caveats I want to be explicit about, because this is the one change here resting on judgement rather than a test:

1. **I don't know `ubuntu-latest-4x`'s actual disk capacity**, so I can't say whether 4x would have failed. This is a hedge against disk exhaustion, not a fix for an observed failure. If you know 4x has the headroom, revert the two lines.
2. **It changes the runner for every image in the repo,** not just this one, since the shared workflow takes a single `amd64-builder`. If you'd rather not move WGCW/WAML/positron-sagemaker onto a bigger runner, the alternative is a separate PR-build invocation for this image — more workflow surface, and I didn't want to restructure `pr.yml` uninvited.

No repo in the org does any disk cleanup (`free-disk-space` and friends appear nowhere in images-shared, images-workbench, or here), so the bigger runner is the only lever that matches existing practice.

## Not in this PR

- **Root `README.md` isn't updated.** Its table is `Platform` / `Platform documentation`, which doesn't fit an image with no host platform, and `positron-sagemaker` isn't listed either. Say the word and I'll add a row or restructure.
- **`positron-sagemaker` is still absent from `release.yml`.** It's on a different versioning scheme (`2026.08.1-2`) with its own `positron-update.yml`, so it's correctly excluded from the Workbench bump — but it means the repo-wide README sed also touches an image the bump doesn't manage. Same class of coupling I fixed for this image; out of scope here.
- **SOCI is off.** Lazy layer pulls would genuinely help at this size and both upstream session images enable it, so it's worth revisiting — left off until the image itself is settled. Noted as such in `bakery.yaml`.
- **The `rstudio-server` UID/GID is unpinned,** faithful to `r-session-complete`, which also lets the postinst pick. Worth flagging that the `workbench` image's uid/gid 999 convention can't just be copied here — in this base gid 999 is already `systemd-journal` and uid 997 is `messagebus`. So pinning is a real decision, not a one-line copy. Documented in the README and the goss comment.

## One reservation about the approach

At 15 GB (Standard) / 13 GB (Minimal) uncompressed, the Workbench payload dominates — Positron Server, `pwb-code-server`, bundled Quarto, Copilot language server. **The Minimal variant buys much less than it normally does**, since ~4.5 GB of IDE payload lands on both. If `min` exists here mainly to be extended, it's still useful; if it exists to be small, it isn't really delivering that, and it may not be worth publishing two variants.

---

title: refactor(positron-sagemaker): remove Secrets Manager licensing, make AWS License Manager required
description:
## Summary

The image was still logging AWS Secrets Manager licensing **errors** despite having migrated to AWS License Manager. Root cause, then removal of the mechanism entirely — the Secrets Manager path was a proof of concept and there is no longer a reason to keep the door open.

Two commits, deliberately kept separate:

1. **`fix:` the log noise** — gates the Secrets Manager bootstrap (the minimal, revertable fix, with before/after evidence)
2. **`refactor:` remove the path** — deletes it outright and makes License Manager required

## The bug

`jupyter_server_config.py` ran the Secrets Manager bootstrap **unconditionally at import time**, ~300 lines above the License Manager client check:

- the license-file install called `_load_license_content()`
- the signing-key load called `_load_signing_key_pem()`

An LM deployment distributes neither a `positron-license` nor a `positron-signing-key` secret, so both lookups always failed, and both logged an ERROR telling the admin to create secrets and grant `secretsmanager:GetSecretValue`. Pure noise: the image was correctly licensed, `positron-server` launched fine via the client, and the suggested remediation was wrong for this deployment.

## What's now gone

`jupyter_server_config.py` loses `_load_signing_key_pem`, `_load_license_content`, the `license.lic` install, `_check_entitlement`, the signing-key load, `_mint_license_token` and the dual-branch command splice — plus the `base64`/`json`/`subprocess`/`datetime` imports and activation-dir constants that existed only to serve them. **The licensing block goes from ~390 lines to ~40**, and `boto3` is no longer imported on the licensing path at all.

## License Manager is now required, not preferred

Since it is the only mechanism left, failures must surface early:

- **Build fails loudly.** The client install is unconditional and its checksum mandatory — a failed download, or a version bump without a matching SHA256, fails the build rather than silently shipping an image that can never license Positron. The `LICENSE_MANAGER_CLIENT_VERSION=""` opt-out is dropped; it only existed to reproduce the signing-key image.
- **Runtime fails clearly.** A missing client is treated as a misbuild and serves the explanatory license-error page instead of launching an unlicensed `positron-server` (which would fail closed as an opaque proxy timeout). The page's copy no longer refers to a signing key.
- **CI catches it.** goss now asserts the client binary is installed and executable.

Also dropped, both dead once minting is gone: the `cryptography` pip pin, and the `chown` of `resources/activation` (it existed so the runtime user could write the Secrets-Manager-fetched `license.lic`).

## Verification

Config loaded under stubs with a `sys.meta_path` hook that blocks *and records* any `boto3` import — a stronger claim than "never called":

| scenario | boto3 imports | licensing ERRORs | `cfg["command"]` |
|---|---|---|---|
| client present | **0** | **0** | list, with `POSITRON_LICENSE_MANAGER_PATH` + `LM_LOG_FILE` spliced |
| client absent | **0** | 1 (explicit misbuild) | callable returning the error-page command |

For reference, the same harness against the pre-fix code with the client present showed **2 Secrets Manager calls and 2 errors** — the exact noise reported.

Completeness check: a repo-wide grep for `secretsmanager` / `POSITRON_SIGNING_KEY` / `POSITRON_LICENSE_SECRET` / `POSITRON_LICENSE_FILE` / `POSITRON_LICENSE_KEY` / `license.lic` / `cryptography` returns **no non-comment hits** under `positron-sagemaker/`. A few comments intentionally retain a one-line historical note. README and the workflows never documented the secrets, so neither needed changes.

Also checked: `py_compile` on both copies, `template/` and `2026.08/` `jupyter_server_config.py` byte-identical, and both Containerfiles' changed lines identical to each other (no jinja content touched).

> [!NOTE]
> The goss assertion swap is the one change that alters the built image beyond dead-code deletion. The removed assertions verified a `chown` that no longer exists; the new one covers the binary that is now the single point of failure for licensing.

title: Wrap rendered diff comment in a code fence
description:
## Problem

The auto-generated **"Rendered file changes"** comment posted by the Positron update workflow (e.g. [PR #64 comment](https://github.com/posit-dev/images-specialized/pull/64#issuecomment-5377934548)) dumps the raw `git diff` output verbatim, with no fenced code block around it.

As a result GitHub renders the diff as ordinary Markdown instead of a code block: no monospace formatting, and `+`/`-` lines get mangled (indentation collapses, `-` lines look like list items).

## Root cause

In `.github/workflows/positron-update.yml`, the *Post or update diff comment* step assembles the body as marker + heading + blank line + `cat "$DIFF_FILE"`, never wrapping the diff in a fence.

## Fix

Wrap the diff in a ````diff``` fenced code block so it renders as a proper diff-highlighted code block.

title: Remove pebble service manager from session-complete images
description:
## What

Removes Canonical's **pebble** service manager from the session-complete images (Ubuntu 26.04, both `-min` and `-std` variants).

## Why

`ubuntu:26.04` ships pebble as a standalone ~10MB binary at `/usr/bin/pebble` (with an empty state tree at `/var/lib/pebble`), and the `workbench-session` base inherits both unchanged. Nothing in a session-complete image uses it:

- the process model is the Job Launcher exec'ing a session per request, not a pebble-supervised service tree;
- neither the base nor this image sets pebble as an entrypoint or references it from `/etc` (verified on both the `-min` and `-std` bases).

So it's dead weight and an unused root-owned service manager on the image's attack surface.

## How

- pebble is **not dpkg-tracked** (no owning package, nothing `Depends` on it), so it can't be removed with `apt-get remove`. The Containerfile deletes the files directly.
- `rm -f` / `rm -rf` keep the step a no-op (not an error) if a future base image stops shipping pebble.
- An explicit post-check fails the build if a future base **relocates** pebble on PATH — a signal to revisit rather than silently reship.
- A goss guard locks the removal in: `exists: false` on both known paths **plus** a `command -v pebble` PATH-level check (catches relocation).

## Files changed

Edits applied to the source-of-truth template, both rendered per-variant Containerfiles, and the template + rendered goss suites:

- `session-complete/template/Containerfile.ubuntu2604.jinja2`
- `session-complete/2026.08/Containerfile.ubuntu2604.min`
- `session-complete/2026.08/Containerfile.ubuntu2604.std`
- `session-complete/template/test/goss.yaml.jinja2`
- `session-complete/2026.08/test/goss.yaml`

## Validation

- Applied the exact removal step against the real `ghcr.io/posit-dev/workbench-session:ubuntu-26.04-min` base: build succeeded, pebble gone from PATH and disk, base (bash, `/opt/R`) intact.
- `pre-commit` passed on the commit.

## Reviewer notes

- [ ] Re-run the Bakery render to confirm the rendered files match the template (the inserted block contains no Jinja, so bodies should be identical).
- [ ] Run `dgoss` on both `-min` and `-std` built images to exercise the new `pebble-service-manager-removed` check.

title: ci: trigger PR checks on merge_group
description:
## Problem

PR #68 hangs forever in the merge queue. The required `CI` check in `.github/workflows/pr.yml` only listens for the `pull_request` event, so when GitHub dispatches a `merge_group` event in the merge queue the workflow never runs and the required check never reports back.

## Fix

Add the `merge_group:` trigger so the same jobs run in the merge queue.

```yaml
on:
  pull_request:
  merge_group:
```

The concurrency group already falls back to `github.run_id` when there is no PR number, so no change needed there.

title: positron-sagemaker: enable SOCI indexing on CI-pushed images
description:
## What

Enables SOCI indexing for the `positron-sagemaker` image so images pushed in CI carry a SOCI index, letting SageMaker Studio / ECR lazily pull layers.

## How

Adopts the org-standard publish/merge flow (the same pattern every images-workbench image uses), applied to this repo's bespoke single-platform workflow:

- **`bakery.yaml`** — enable the `soci` tool option on `positron-sagemaker` (`tool: soci, enabled: true`).
- **`positron-sagemaker.yml`**
  - The `build` job's push step now builds with `--strategy build --push --temp-registry ghcr.io/posit-dev --metadata-file …`, publishing per-platform **temp** images to ghcr and recording build metadata (uploaded as an artifact). It no longer creates the final product tags, so it no longer needs AWS credentials — the `sagemaker-distribution` base still pulls anonymously from ECR Public.
  - New **`merge`** job (`environment: production`) logs into ghcr + public ECR, installs `oras` + `soci`, downloads the metadata, and runs `bakery ci publish` — `oras index-create → soci-convert → oras index-copy` — which applies the SOCI index and lands the result on the real ghcr + `public.ecr.aws` tags.
  - The required `ci` meta-job now also needs `merge`, with `allowed-skips: merge` (merge is skipped on PR builds, which push nothing).

Push gating is unchanged: temp push + merge run only on merges to `main`, the weekly schedule, and `workflow_dispatch` on `main`. PR builds still only build + test locally.

## Notes / follow-ups (not in this PR)

- **No `clean.yml` in this repo.** `bakery ci publish` intentionally leaves temp indexes in the temp registry for an out-of-band `bakery clean temp-registry` job to reap (as in images-workbench). Without one, temp tags will accumulate under `ghcr.io/posit-dev`. Worth adding a clean workflow as a follow-up.
- **Double build.** The `build` job builds once with the `bake` strategy (`--load`, for the dgoss test) and again with the `build` strategy for the temp push; the buildkit layer cache is shared, so the second pass is mostly cache hits.

## Testing

- `bakery.yaml` and the workflow parse cleanly (`bakery ci matrix`, `bakery ci publish --help`).
- pre-commit (actionlint, zizmor, yaml, etc.) passes on both changed files.

title: fix: restore the exec bit on session-complete's install script
description:
`session-complete/2026.08/scripts/install_workbench.sh` starts with a shebang but was mode `100644`, which fails pre-commit's `check-shebang-scripts-are-executable`. That hook feeds `Lint`, and `Lint` feeds the required `CI` gate, so `main` and every open PR have been red since the 2026.08.2 release.

The rendered script was added at `100755` and was correct. Its template was added at `100644`, and Bakery renders with the template's mode, so the first re-render of the version directory — the 2026.08.2 release — dropped the bit. Fixing only the rendered file would regress at the next release, so both get it. Every other image in this repository already has `100755` on both.

This is mode-only; there is no content change, and no effect on the image. The Containerfile does `COPY --chmod=0755`, so the script has always been executable at build time. The failure was lint-only.

No pre-commit config change is needed, and adding an exclude would mask the bug rather than fix it. `check-executables-have-shebangs` already excludes `^.*\.sh\.jinja2$`, which covers the now-executable template (it opens with a Jinja comment, not a shebang). `check-shebang-scripts-are-executable` needs no exclude, because the template has no shebang for it to match on. That is the same hook configuration `images-workbench`, `images-connect`, and `images-package-manager` use.

This unblocks the queue for all open PRs, including:

- https://github.com/posit-dev/images-specialized/pull/74

title: ci: build only the images a push actually changed
description:
Each per-image workflow triggered on every push to `main` and rebuilt its image unconditionally, so a change confined to one image still burned runner time on the other three. The product image repos already avoid this via `bakery ci matrix --base-ref`, which maps a push's changed files onto the image/version matrix and returns an empty matrix when nothing relevant was touched. These workflows hand-roll their matrix job rather than calling the shared workflow, so the same pattern is applied inline.

- `BASE_REF` is gated on `github.event_name == 'push'`, so scheduled weekly rebuilds and manual dispatches still build the full matrix.
- Matrix checkouts use `fetch-depth: 0` so the diff can reach the base ref.
- Build jobs (and Positron SageMaker's merge job) are guarded on a non-empty matrix, because Actions fails rather than skips a matrix job when the matrix is `[]`.
- The `matrix` job joins each `CI` gate's `needs` so that allowing a skipped `build` cannot mask a matrix failure.

Also fixes a latent failure in the same step. It wrote its output as `echo "matrix=$(bakery ... | jq ...)"`; a command substitution used as an argument cannot fail the step under `set -e`, and these workflows never set `defaults.run.shell`, so they ran under GitHub's default `bash -e` with pipefail off. Neither stage of that pipeline was guarded, so a crashing `bakery` produced a green matrix job and a confusing `fromJson('')` error in the build job. The pipeline is now assigned to a variable under `shell: bash`, matching `images-shared`.

Note that merging this rebuilds all four images once: `.github/workflows/` is in bakery's full-build fallback list, so a workflow change forces a full matrix. One-time and self-correcting.

Closes https://github.com/posit-dev/images-specialized/issues/73

title: feat(positron-sagemaker): add paws R package to the default image
description:
## What

Adds the [`paws`](https://paws-r.github.io/) R package — the AWS SDK for R — to the default R package set in the Positron on SageMaker image.

## Why

Users on SageMaker routinely reach for AWS services (S3, Athena, Bedrock, Secrets Manager) from R. Without `paws` in the image they install it themselves into a home directory that a Space recreates, so the install does not persist across Spaces.

## How

One package added to the existing P3M install layer, so it arrives as a prebuilt binary rather than compiling from source:

```r
install.packages(c("IRkernel", "tidyverse", "data.table", "shiny", "odbc", "DBI", "paws"), ...)
```

Both files are updated, since both are tracked here:

- `positron-sagemaker/template/Containerfile.ubuntu2404.jinja2` — the `r.run_install_packages` call
- `positron-sagemaker/2026.08/Containerfile.ubuntu2404` — the rendered output

## Testing notes

`paws` is pure R with no compiled code, so it needs no additional system libraries and the goss `r-packages-system-libraries-resolve` check is unaffected. No apt, goss, or enforced-settings changes.

Not built locally — `pre-commit` and `bakery` were not installed in this environment, so the rendered file was edited to match what the template macro produces rather than regenerated. Worth confirming CI's render check agrees.

One thing for the reviewer to weigh: `paws` is a metapackage that pulls the full set of `paws.*` service bindings, which adds meaningful size to an image already around 16 GB uncompressed. If that is a concern, `paws.common` plus a targeted subset (e.g. `paws.storage`, `paws.analytics`) would be lighter.
